items.title: Molmo 2 | Robotics Applications
items.summary:
Researcher Jiafei Dua demonstrates some of Molmo 2’s potential applications for robotics research. 

Molmo 2 is a state-of-the-art open multimodal model suite capable of precise spatial and temporal understanding of video, image, and multi-image sets. Building on the global impact of Molmo, which pioneered image pointing for multimodal AI systems, Molmo 2 introduces breakthrough capabilities in video pointing, multi-frame reasoning, and object tracking. 

Learn more: allenai.org/molmo 
Discuss in Discord:  discord.gg/Ai2

items.title: Applied Materials Accelerates Chip Manufacturing With NVIDIA
items.summary:
See how Applied Materials and NVIDIA are transforming chipmaking, as Applied Materials uses #digitaltwins built on #NVIDIAOmniverse libraries to simulate fab‑level optimizations in layout, throughput, cost, and process control. 

With accelerated computing and NVIDIA cuDSS library, Applied’s ACE+ and Ginestra modules speed these simulations by up to 35x and 10x, cutting runtimes from days or months to hours or minutes.

items.title: OpenAI at $500B: The Path to a $1 Trillion IPO Revealed AMAZON
items.summary:
A new power axis is forming in the global AI stack, and the numbers are staggering. 📉📈 Tonight, we break down the exclusive reports that Amazon is in talks to invest over $10 billion in OpenAI, a move that could skyrocket the ChatGPT maker's valuation past $500 billion.

But this isn't just about money. It’s a calculated strike in the "Chip Wars." For the first time, OpenAI is signaling a major break from its single-cloud dependency on Microsoft. By potentially adopting Amazon’s proprietary Trainium chips, this deal directly challenges Nvidia’s dominance and validates Amazon's silicon strategy at the highest level.

In this video, we analyze:
The Deal: Inside the $10B investment and the path to a $1 Trillion IPO. 
The Shift: Why OpenAI is diversifying beyond Microsoft Azure. 
The Chip War: How Amazon Trainium could disrupt Nvidia's monopoly. 
The Infrastructure Phase: Why the next decade of AI is about owning the stack—Compute, Chips, Cloud, and Capital.

Is this the beginning of the end for Nvidia's total dominance? Or just the next phase of the AI bubble?

items.title: India ($0.7T) vs China ($4.9T) | The Manufacturing Truth No One Tells You
items.summary:
India has just crossed a historic milestone. 🇮🇳 We are officially the 5th largest manufacturing power in the world, overtaking industrial giants like the UK, France, Italy, and South Korea. With a manufacturing output of $781 Billion, India has entered the global super league.

But headlines don’t tell the full story. In this episode of Front Page, we expose the "dirty secret" of global manufacturing: Output is NOT Ownership. While we are producing millions of phones and cars, a painful 60-70% of the value—the profit, the IP, and the margins—still flies back to foreign countries. We are hosting the feast, but are we just washing the dishes?

In this video, we analyze: 
The Ranking: How India climbed to #5. 
The Reality Check: Comparing India’s $781B against China’s massive $4.9T output. 
The Value Trap: Why "Made in India" often means "Assembled in India" (and why that needs to change). 
The Solution: How we move from buying machines to building them.


Don't forget to Like, Share, and Subscribe to Front Page by AIM Network!

This is the most critical economic shift of the decade. Can India move from being the world’s workshop to the world’s laboratory?

India has just crossed a historic milestone. 🇮🇳 We are officially the 5th largest manufacturing power in the world, overtaking industrial giants like the UK, France, Italy, and South Korea. With a manufacturing output of $781 Billion, India has entered the global super league.

But headlines don’t tell the full story. In this episode of Front Page, we expose the "dirty secret" of global manufacturing: Output is NOT Ownership. While we are producing millions of phones and cars, a painful 60-70% of the value—the profit, the IP, and the margins—still flies back to foreign countries. We are hosting the feast, but are we just washing the dishes?

In this video, we analyze: 
The Ranking: How India climbed to #5. 
The Reality Check: Comparing India’s $781B against China’s massive $4.9T output. 
The Value Trap: Why "Made in India" often means "Assembled in India" (and why that needs to change). 
The Solution: How we move from buying machines to building them.


Don't forget to Like, Share, and Subscribe to Front Page by AIM Network!

This is the most critical economic shift of the decade. Can India move from being the world’s workshop to the world’s laboratory?
👇 Let us know in the comments: Do you think India can crack the "component" market in the next 5 years?

items.title: NHK Broadcasting Technology Research Laboratory's AI Technology Development Initiatives
items.summary:
NHK produces a wide range of content, including dramas, news, educational programs, and documentaries, and there is a growing need to streamline the production of this content. The NHK Broadcasting Technology Research Laboratory is engaged in research and development of AI technologies capable of processing diverse modalities such as text, images, audio, and sign language, aiming to enhance content production efficiency. Furthermore, to enhance safety in operational use within broadcasting stations, we are also advancing the development of our own large-scale language models. This presentation will introduce our institute's AI technology development initiatives, including large-scale language model development, and their application in broadcasting operations.

--

NHKは、ドラマ・ニュース・教育番組・ドキュメンタリーなど多岐にわたるコンテンツを制作しており、これらのコンテンツ制作の効率化が求められています。NHK放送技術研究所では、コンテンツ制作の効率向上を目指し、テキスト・画像・音声・手話など多様なモダリティを処理できるAI技術の研究開発に取り組んでいます。さらに、放送局での業務利用における安全性を高めるため、独自の大規模言語モデルの開発も進めています。本講演では、当研究所による大規模言語モデルの開発をはじめとするAI技術開発の取り組みと放送業務での活用についてご紹介します。

items.title: Yali Capital's DEEP TECH Strategy: Investing in IP & Founder Technical Depth
items.summary:
Welcome to an exclusive interview with Karthikeyan Madathil, Partner at Yali Capital, to discuss the rigorous investment thesis driving the Deep Tech ecosystem in India. From his early career as a chip designer at Texas Instruments to co-founding an ML-powered edtech company, Madathil shares the engineering instincts that now guide his investment strategy. Yali Capital focuses exclusively on Deep Tech startups, believing the Indian ecosystem has reached the maturity level needed for substantive, IP-led growth.

To evaluate startups, the firm conducts in-depth technical reviews that extend beyond the pitch deck. The objective is to understand not only what the founders know but also what they are aware they do not know about the problem they are trying to solve.

The discussion covers Yali's key portfolio bets, showcasing their diversity across Deep Tech verticals. These include Health Tech (precision genomics for late-stage cancer care, e.g., Foresee Medical), Robotics (humanoid and semi-humanoid robots, e.g., Perceptron), and Semiconductor (chip design solutions such as C2I for the complex power-supply needs of GPUs and high-performance CPUs). In AI Applications, they favour custom approaches, such as those from Point AI, for 2D/3D image generation, rather than relying solely on Generative AI.

Looking ahead, Karthikeyan Madathil addresses the systemic issues that are slowing India's Deep Tech future. He highlights the need for more late-stage capital and streamlined processes to navigate compliance. Furthermore, he emphasises that India must solve its crucial "chicken and egg" problem to build a strong indigenous supply chain, especially in semiconductors, and argues for policy support to stimulate demand for domestic startups.

items.title: AI Fails Because It Doesn't Understand How People Really Work (with Alex "Sandy" Pentland)
items.summary:
Alex “Sandy” Pentland, Toshiba Professor of Media Arts & Science at MIT and Fellow at Stanford, speaks to @JonKrohnLearns about his new book, Shared Wisdom, why he attributes AI to the collapse of the Soviet Union, and why those risks to society could still be relevant today. We can only achieve better system performance, Alex says, when we build tools that keep step with the way that people make decisions. Listen to the episode to hear Alex talk about how he is helping make AI agents work for individuals rather than the companies that develop them, and his work in making sure that systems operate consistently and fairly across the world.

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/949

items.title: Google’s $12M Bet, Sanskrit LLM Launch, Tata’s AI City, and India’s First 64-Bit CPU
items.summary: India’s AI momentum hit a new peak this week. Google committed $12M+ to Indian AI research, health foundation models, Indic-language tech, and clean-energy compute. India began building its first Sanskrit LLM, digitising 110,000+ texts to create a culturally rooted AI model. Tata Group announced a massive Uttar Pradesh expansion — including an AI City in Lucknow, 30,000+ tech jobs, defence manufacturing, and new power infrastructure. And C-DAC unveiled DHRUV64, India’s first fully indigenous 64-bit, 1.0 GHz microprocessor under the RISC-V programme. Together, these moves signal India’s shift from AI adoption to AI creation — across silicon, language, infrastructure, and public systems.

items.title: Google’s $12M Bet on India: Beating Microsoft & Amazon?, Invests Big in Corover.ai
items.summary:
Global Big Tech’s battle for India has shifted gears, with Google announcing a massive $12 million commitment to fuel the nation’s AI ecosystem, a move distinct from the infrastructure-heavy plays of Microsoft and Amazon. At its 'Lab to Impact' dialogue, Google revealed a strategy deeply integrated with India’s public systems, funding everything from 'MedGemma' for healthcare foundation models to AI Centres of Excellence at top IITs and IISc. This initiative goes beyond mere code; it includes a critical $4.5 million grant to Wadhwani AI for empowering frontline health and agriculture workers, a new Indic Language hub at IIT Bombay, and a 150 MW solar partnership with ReNew to ensure this digital growth is sustainable. This is Google betting not just on Indian startups, but on the foundational AI layers that will run the country’s health, education, and energy sectors for decades to come.

items.title: How Robotaxis Are Gaining Ground to Make Streets Safer
items.summary:
🚕 Robotaxis are moving from pilots to real streets.

From Austin and Dallas to Las Vegas and beyond, industry leaders explain how autonomous vehicles are scaling safely—using real-world data, simulation, and AI built for edge cases.

Hear from Uber, Avride, and Zoox on what it takes to commercialize robotaxis and raise the safety bar for urban mobility.

▶️ Watch the full video: https://nvda.ws/48GfItM
